decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: P1 'Save a bookmark — URL, optional title & notes; validates the address; persists across reloads'. Client (round 1): 'I approve the specification as-is.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. Saving a bookmark by URL conforms to the reference; recorded conforming decision, not a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope decision: 'No auto-fetching of page titles or favicons (titles are user-entered)'. Client (round 1): 'I approve the specification as-is. Please proceed to planning.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. Reference REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title/description/favicon/preview on save; the presentation explicitly excludes this. Divergence established from the spec; client gave bare approval with no expression of the difference, so it passes unexpressed. The maker even flagged 'auto-fetched titles' as a possible request, yet the client did not raise it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope decision: 'No browser import/export'. Client (round 1): 'I approve the specification as-is.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. Reference REF-BM-30/31 require Netscape HTML import and export; presentation excludes both as a single scope decision. Divergence established independently; bare approval expresses no awareness of the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: 'duplicate URLs warn but don't block' (restated round 4: 'non-blocking duplicate warning'). Client (round 2): 'The plan sounds appropriate. I approve it; please proceed to the task breakdown.'
decisions.note: Plan gate. Reference REF-BM-06 requires re-saving an existing URL to converge on editing the existing bookmark (preventing duplicates); the presented behaviour permits creating duplicates with only a warning. Divergence established from the reference; bare approval, no expression of the difference. Restated at round 4 acceptance without change — counted once at first presentation to avoid double-counting.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker offered alternatives: option 1 'proceed... build the app against these tasks' vs option 2 'tell me to limit implementation to the MVP (US1) first', with 'Suggested MVP scope: Phases 1+2+3 (US1)'. Client (round 3): 'I approve the task breakdown. Please implement the full planned app, including all four user stories, rather than stopping at the MVP.'
decisions.note: Tasks gate. The offered MVP-only alternative would drop US2 browse/search, US3 edit/delete, and US4 tags — i.e. reference items REF-BM-04/05/07/08/09/11/12. The alternatives differ in fulfilment of reference functional items, so the offered decision is marked diverged=true; the client explicitly selected the reference-conforming (fuller) alternative. This is the one active co-construction capture, catch_type=select.
